releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 10
releases.body:
# AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 10

Beta 10 adds **global physical-controller profiles** and improves Mophun sound and game speed.

Open **Settings → Physical controller profiles** to edit the global mapping or create reusable profiles for buttons and both sticks. Assign them to games from the manager or each game's Controls page. Graphics, touch layouts and physical mappings stay independent. Existing per-game overrides take priority; shared changes apply the next time the game opens. Profiles are included in library backups.

Mophun sound is now enabled for every game. Short BEEP effects and `vBeep` are supported, and PCM follows pause and emulation speed. A common phone-model execution budget reduces excessive speed in CPU-dependent games such as the supplied Boulder Dash and Lemtris versions.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.10.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and experimental Symbian/N-Gage.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.10-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Android 10+ is required. Both update the existing app in place. Back up important saves before updating or switching architecture. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 9
releases.body:
Beta 9 adds **independent right-stick mapping** for physical controllers.

Open **Controls → Controller mapping → Sticks** to assign the right stick’s directions and diagonals to phone keys, soft keys or Fire. **Identify** detects right-stick movement; pressing R3 remains a separate input. Bindings are saved per game, and existing profiles keep their settings with the new directions unbound.

The shared input path supports Java ME, Mophun and Symbian/N-Gage. This maps stick directions to digital keys; it does not add proportional analog camera support to games.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.9.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and experimental Symbian/N-Gage.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.9-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Android 10+ is required. Both update the existing app in place.

Tested with automated input and a virtual joystick on Retroid; physical dual-stick hardware testing remains pending. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 8
releases.body:
Beta 8 fixes Lara's black/striped appearance and loading-screen text showing through her model in **Tomb Raider: Underworld 3D**. The cause was incorrect transparency when transferring M3G rendering to the Java ME screen.

Startup errors now show the original game exception instead of only `InvocationTargetException`.

- **ARM64:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.8.apk` — Java ME, Mophun and the combined Symbian runtime.
- **ARMv7:** `AbyssME-0.7.0-beta.8-armv7.apk` — Java ME and Mophun, without Symbian.

Both require Android 10+ and update the existing app without uninstalling.

The reported **Crash Titans 1.3.7 Sony S700i JAR** was also checked. Its code and packed resources are inconsistent; the same reader fails on ordinary Java outside AbyssME. This release does not make that particular JAR playable.

Checks: 427 JVM tests per build, focused Retroid renderer tests, signed APK update and first-room checks. This is not complete-game acceptance. Source bundles and SHA-256 checksums are included.

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 7
releases.body:
# AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 7

## Separate graphics and control profiles

- **Settings → Graphics profiles** and **Settings → Control profiles** now have
  independent global defaults, named profiles and assignments. Each game can
  select one graphics profile and one control profile. Changing or resetting
  one category leaves the other intact; extra Gamepad buttons remain available.
- Graphics profiles include supported scaling, smoothing, built-in xBRZ/CRT,
  FSR/sharpness, interpolation, LCD filters and capture settings. Java GPU and
  Mophun support GPU effects; Symbian uses its supported host display options.
  Integer scaling falls back to Fit on Symbian. Java-only geometry options are
  identified in the editor's support information.
- Beta 6 combined profiles split automatically: LCD inheritance and exceptions
  move to graphics, while touch settings remain in controls. Other existing
  graphics remain explicit overrides. Reset the relevant category's overrides
  when you want existing games to inherit a shared setup.
- Both catalogs, including unassigned profiles, travel through library backups.
  Phone backups retain portable game definitions. Picture Keep/Undo preserves

releases.name: AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 6
releases.body:
# AbyssME 0.7.0 Beta 6

## Shared profiles and extra touch buttons

- Set global touch/LCD defaults and create named profiles from **Settings →
  Profiles / Global defaults**. Link individual games or assign a profile to
  several prepared games. Edit a shared profile once; linked games use it on
  their next launch.
- Keep per-game exceptions, inspect which profile supplies each setting, and
  reset individual overrides. Existing game settings stay unchanged on upgrade;
  explicitly reset their touch/LCD overrides to adopt shared settings.
- Add up to twelve independent Gamepad buttons in **Edit touch layout → Extra**.
  Choose a key and label, size, opacity and separate portrait/landscape positions.
  Additional buttons are included in shared profiles.
- Library backups carry profile definitions and assignments. Phone backups carry
  portable per-game definitions. Restore preserves destination profiles when
  names or identities conflict.

[Usage and scope](https://github.com/EriArk/JavaEmulator/blob/main/docs/SHARED_PROFILES.md) · [Verification](https://github.com/EriArk/JavaEmulator/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.7.0-beta.6-checks.md).

releases.name: Anka Native 0.3.0
releases.body:
Anka Native 0.3.0 draws the tree canopies, plants and the arch beside Link's door that 0.2.2 left out, adds a 3D resolution setting, a faster Prepare on the phone and three new languages.
It is still slow: Kokiri Forest runs at about 14 fps on our test phone, and frames are slower than in 0.2.2 where the new content is on screen. The change for the Adreno 840 hang (#5) is untested because we have no Adreno 840.

"Tested on the phone" below means our only test phone: POCO F8 Pro (Adreno 830, 12 GB, Android 16 / HyperOS). "Tests only" means automated tests or a computer, not a phone.

### What is new

- **Mesh-drawn content is now drawn.** Kokiri Forest's tree canopies, grass, ferns, flowers and the arch beside Link's door, and the Deku Tree upper floor's floor that was invisible ([#6](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/6)). 0.2.2 skipped these draws on Turnip drivers. Your pack gets the needed shaders through an automatic update (see *After updating*). Tested on the phone with Anka Turnip: no draws skipped in Kokiri Forest and the Deku Tree's upper floor. Not tested on an Adreno 7xx, and not with Qualcomm's own driver.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.2
releases.body:
### Security fix

- **The launcher no longer takes control commands from other apps** ([#7](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/7)).
  - Before this release, any app on the phone could ask Anka Native's launcher to install or pick a GPU driver, add a game, start Prepare, or export or import a pack. These are commands meant for testing over adb.
  - The app now ignores them and shows a short message, unless you turn on **Settings › ADB control (debug)**. That switch is off by default and asks before it turns on. Turn it on only while you use adb.
  - Starting a game from a frontend works as before.

Everything else is as in [0.2.1](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/releases/tag/v0.2.1). The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG_ANKA_NATIVE.md](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/blob/main/CHANGELOG_ANKA_NATIVE.md).

### Files

- `anka-native-0.2.2.apk`: the app (`dev.ankanative.android`), signed with the release key. Certificate SHA-256: `4d7443354f53a0aef11bc4df1a34ff3fc5bd6d748bbeb76fd78c80a6841f3bb0`. It installs over earlier versions and keeps your saves.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt`: checksum of the APK

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.1
releases.body:
### Fixes

- **Prepare on the phone stopped at the end for Ocarina of Time** ([#3](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/3)): "76 of 42346 shaders did not build: no library written".

  The same 76 shaders don't build on a computer either, and the game runs without them. Ocarina of Time's profile was missing the list that tells the phone which shaders those are, so the phone counted them as failures. 0.2.1 adds the list.

  Checked on a computer with the phone's rule: the library is now written, byte for byte the one a computer makes.

  **If your Prepare stopped with this message:** update to 0.2.1, open the game's card and tap **Retry**. The shaders already translated are kept, so it only tries the 76 again and then writes the library.

### New

- **Prepare on a computer on Windows** too, besides Linux and the Mac. Setup: [android/README.md](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/blob/main/android/README.md#the-environment).
- **[Discussions](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/discussions)** are open. Tell us how it runs on your phone in the [device reports](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/discussions/1) thread.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.0
releases.body:
**Prepare on the phone (experimental).** The app can now make a game's pack from your dump on the phone itself. You no longer need a computer.

### How

Copy your dump (or `.nup`) to the phone, open **Anka Native**, tap **Add game**, pick the dump and tap **Prepare**. The app does three things in the background, with a notification:

1. It rewrites the game's code.
2. It scans the game's files for shaders.
3. It translates the shaders.

When it is done, the game's card says Ready.

- **Keep the phone on a charger.** For Ocarina of Time, preparing takes about 3 hours and uses the CPU fully.
- If a step fails, the card says why. Its log is in `<title ID>-work/ondevice/logs` next to the dump. Preparing on a computer still works as before.

### What was tested

On a POCO F8 Pro with Ocarina of Time:

- **Code rewrite:** worked, about 3 minutes.
- **Shader scan:** worked, about 35 minutes for the game's 186,583 files. It found 42,346 shaders, as many as on a computer.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.1.1
releases.body:
A fix for 0.1.0: **Prepare on the phone looked done but made nothing to play.**

0.1.0 was built without the on-phone packer. Its Prepare ran a simulated engine: the progress finished, but the pack it made was an empty placeholder with no game code and no shaders, so Play could not start the game.

### What changed

- Without the on-phone packer, the app no longer offers Prepare. Home and the game's card now say to prepare the game on a computer (the README's [Install](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative#install) steps) and to pick that pack.
- A placeholder pack left by 0.1.0 is no longer shown as ready: the card says "No pack", and Play explains why.

Preparing on the phone itself is being worked on for a later release.

Everything else is as in [0.1.0](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/releases/tag/v0.1.0): your own dump is needed, the driver is [Anka Turnip 1.0.0](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaTurnip/releases/tag/v1.0.0), and the RAM saver is recommended below 16 GB of RAM. Tested only on a POCO F8 Pro with Ocarina of Time.

### Files

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.9.5
releases.body: # ARMSX2 2.9.5 What's new: ## Memory cards **Folder memory cards keep every save.** If your memory card's Type is Folder, every save is now written whole. A save made just before you left the app could come back blank or as the older version, because the card was written to storage between the save's data and its file entry; that can no longer happen. A new save that reuses a deleted save's space keeps its own name instead of reappearing under the deleted one's. A save file the device won't open for writing is still read, where the game showed it as damaged. New saves are created on storage that needs Android's own file access with the IOP thread on, and leaving the app rewrites nothing when nothing on the card changed. done by @bmdhacks

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.9.4
releases.body: # ARMSX2 2.9.4 ## New **Vulkan by default.** New installs start on the Vulkan renderer on every device whose driver reports Vulkan 1.1, and on Auto elsewhere. Existing installs keep the renderer they have. Auto now picks Vulkan on every Mali of the Bifrost G31, G51, G52 and G76 generation and of the Valhall generations (G57 to G78, G310 to G710, G615, G715, Immortalis-G715). done by @bmdhacks **MaliSX2 on every Mali it drives.** The GPU Driver list, the GPU card, first-run setup and the driver notice offer MaliSX2 on the Mali-G31, G51, G52 and G76, G57, G68, G77 and G78, G310, G510, G610 and G710, and G615, G715 and Immortalis-G715. The G31, G51 and G310 to G710 need MaliSX2 0.5.0 or newer. done by @bmdhacks

releases.name: ARMSX2 nightly 20261114 (6d9511e29e)
releases.body:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.

There is also [a beta release](https://github.com/Borked3DS/Borked3DS/releases/tag/v2025.01.23-sdl-compat) that is the same as this one except that it incorporates the use of SDL3 via the SDL2 compatability layer. The intent is to port this project over to pure SDL3 eventually, but the compatability layer approach allows people to play around with things while waiting for the porting to be completed. This also gives this project a fallback in case SDL2 stops being supported upstream but new functionality such as gamepad support for new game controllers continues to be updated on the SDL3 branch.

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.16
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.16: LAN sin bloqueos y reportes más completos

### Cambios

- **Crear carrera LAN ya no detiene el juego si tu `server.dll` es de otra versión.** Antes salía "Arranque guest detenido: server.dll: file layout does not match the lifted code" y el juego se paraba. Ahora aparece un aviso: ese teléfono no puede crear la carrera, pero sí unirse a una que cree otro jugador. Para crearla, copia el `server.dll` de la misma instalación de PC de donde sacaste el ejecutable del juego.
- **Rendimiento recuperado en procesadores con solo 2 núcleos rápidos** (Helio G85/G88, MT6769 y similares). Desde la versión anterior, todos los hilos del juego se fijaban a los núcleos rápidos. En estos procesadores eso los metía todos en solo 2 núcleos, y el juego iba peor que antes. Ahora solo se fijan cuando hay al menos 4 núcleos rápidos; si no, Android los reparte como antes.

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.15
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.15: driver recomendado para tu GPU

### Driver Vulkan recomendado para tu procesador

- **El launcher te dice qué driver usar.** En *Opciones › Driver Vulkan* ahora aparece la GPU de tu teléfono y el driver que le conviene:
  - **Snapdragon (Adreno 6xx/7xx):** Turnip (Mesa), si el driver del sistema va lento o con errores gráficos.
  - **MediaTek, Exynos, Tensor o Unisoc con Mali-G57 o más nueva:** PanVK (Mesa), con la misma condición.
  - **Mali-G52/G72/G76 o más antiguas:** el driver del sistema (PanVK aún es experimental en ellas).
  - **PowerVR (Moto g54, Helio G35/G37…) y Samsung Xclipse:** el driver del sistema. No hay un driver alternativo que funcione en ellas.
- **Aviso si el driver no es para tu GPU.** Si eliges un driver hecho para otra GPU (por ejemplo, Turnip en una Mali o PanVK en una Adreno), el launcher avisa de que el juego probablemente no arrancará.

La app no incluye ningún driver: los importas tú como ZIP (adrenotools) desde el mismo diálogo.

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.14
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.14: volver al juego sin cierres y reportes completos

Revisamos los reportes de la v0.1.13. La protección para GPU PowerVR funcionó: el Moto g54 ya pasa del primer dibujo. Esta versión corrige el cierre más repetido y hace que los reportes traigan la información que necesitamos.

### Correcciones

- **Cierre al volver al juego.** Si salías a otra app y volvías, el juego podía cerrarse en el primer fotograma. Android libera la ventana del juego al pasar a segundo plano, pero la superficie Vulkan seguía usándola y se destruía después. Ahora la superficie conserva su ventana hasta que se destruye.

### Reportes más útiles

- **El resumen del issue ya trae las líneas del juego.** Antes se tomaban de logcat y, cuando pulsabas *Reportar*, Android ya las había borrado: casi todos los issues llegaban con "últimas líneas del juego" vacío. Ahora salen del registro propio del juego (`game.log`), y logcat solo aporta las líneas del cierre.

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.13
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.13: mega actualización

Revisamos uno por uno los reportes y los zip de diagnóstico que nos enviaron. Esta versión corrige los fallos más repetidos y añade lo necesario para que los próximos reportes traigan toda la información.

### Gráficos

- **Detalle de las sombras ya se puede activar.** El juego solo habilita esa opción con tarjetas NVIDIA o ATI. Ahora el port se presenta como una NVIDIA GeForce 7800 GTX, así que la opción se puede subir y las sombras se dibujan en carrera.
- **Texturas DXT1 con transparencia correcta.** Se convierten a A1R5G5B5, como ya hace Carbon: menos memoria y bordes recortados correctos.
- **Protección para GPU PowerVR (MediaTek, p. ej. Moto g54 / Dimensity 7020).** El driver Vulkan de MediaTek se caía al crear el primer pipeline gráfico, en los cuatro juegos. Ahora, si el driver falla, el port reintenta con configuraciones más simples hasta encontrar una que funcione. *No hemos podido probarlo en un teléfono PowerVR; si tienes uno, cuéntanos cómo va.*

### Estabilidad

releases.name: DolphinVR Redux v0.5 - The Fall Update
releases.body:
DolphinVR Redux v0.5 brings VR game patches, which put your hands and your head into the games themselves, an in-game menu you use without taking the headset off, a large round of Meta Quest performance work, and automatic updates on Windows.

## Highlights

- **VR game patches.** The arm cannon follows your controller in the Metroid Prime games, the gun and sword follow it in Red Steel 1 and 2, Skyward Sword reads your controller's true pose, and Twilight Princess, The Wind Waker, Wii Sports and Shadow the Hedgehog can be played in first person.
- **An in-game VR menu.** Click the left thumbstick during a game to pause, fast forward, change settings, rebind controls, manage savestates and hunt overrides, all inside the headset.
- **Faster on Meta Quest.** Super Mario Galaxy went from 42 to 60 fps and Super Mario Sunshine from 49 to 60 fps at native resolution in my tests with "Smart Foveation EFB".
- **Automatic updates on Windows.** This is the first version that updates itself. See "Installing" below.
- **Rebased on the latest Dolphin** development builds (October 2026).

## VR game patches

releases.name: DolphinVR Redux v0.4 — The Summer Update
releases.body:
DolphinVR Redux v0.4 introduces new graphics backends, major OpenXR improvements, Meta Quest passthrough support, expanded VR configuration tools, and a wide range of rendering and stability fixes.

Highlights

- Added DirectX 12 and OpenGL renderer support.
- Added OpenXR asynchronous mode for Vulkan and DirectX 12.
- Added passthrough support for Meta Quest headsets.
- Added foveated rendering to improve performance on Quest.
- Introduced a new VR configuration panel for binding controls directly in VR.
- Improved the Texture Override, Hide Code, and Shader Hunter tools.


OpenXR and VR

- Added OpenXR asynchronous mode for Vulkan and DirectX 12.
- Added an eager frame heartbeat for native VR frame-rate operation.
- Added a new VR configuration panel for controller bindings.
- Added new camera and controller anchor overrides.
- Added a new "Screen pane" override.
- Updated the Wiimote pointer to use absolute pointing.
- Fixed Wii MotionPlus gyroscope behavior.

Meta Quest

- Added passthrough support for Meta Quest headsets.
- Added foveated rendering to improve performance.
- Added a new first-launch screen for applying recommended Quest bindings.

releases.name: Dolphin VR Redux v0.3 — The Metroid Update
releases.body:
This update brings a major round of improvements, with a strong focus on Metroid Prime, element overrides, Vulkan rendering, and overall performance.

- All major Metroid Prime fixes from the 2016 DolphinVR-Hydra branch have now been ported and integrated, including: Detect Skybox, Remove Cinematic Bars, 3D HUD, Visor EFB Skips...

- These fixes have also been improved with additional work, such as the Layered Palette Conversion Path, which restores the thermal, X-Ray, dark, and scanner visor effects in Metroid Prime 1, 2, and 3

- Added Headlock HUD support for Metroid Prime Trilogy

- Fixed the Element Override Tool, which can now finally work with projection-based definition overrides

- Added a new Texture Element Override system that, unlike shader-based overrides, uses the texture hash to identify elements. It is easier to use and should remain persistent across versions

- Updated Vulkan with new fixes; it now uses full projection for every headset

- Improved performance through multiple bug fixes.

- Also includes an experimental release for Meta Quest 3 and Debian Linux

releases.name: v1.0.8
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.8: big games run much faster

### What's new
- **Games with very large buffers run much faster.** 1.0.7 uploaded every recently used buffer whole each frame, which for a game like Teardown meant over 3 GB per frame. Now only small buffers (up to 4 MB) are uploaded that way; large ones are tracked by page again. Teardown on a PS4 Pro went from under 1 FPS to about 2.4 FPS. DREDGE keeps its 1.0.7 speed and clean sound.
- **A new emulator build** (KytyPS5 589bd14 with EmuFive patches 0001–0032).

### Teardown and other big games: more GPU memory
Teardown also needs the GPU to be allowed up to 5 GB of system RAM, or it stops with GPU out of memory. Use the `bootargs.txt` of [PS4 Multiboot v1.5.0-beta-5](https://github.com/blue0x1/ps4-multiboot/releases/tag/v1.5.0-beta.5) (copy it to `/data/linux/boot/` over FTP), or add `amdgpu.gttsize=5120 ttm.pages_limit=1310720` to the end of the line in your own.

### Update
Settings, System, Software update. No restart is needed. Coming from 1.0.6 or earlier, it installs 1.0.7 first, which also updates the PS4 Mesa (see the 1.0.7 notes).

From 1.0.3 or earlier, start the update once by hand (see the README's Changelog).

releases.name: v1.0.7
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.7: faster games, smooth cover changes

### What's new
- **Faster games.** The emulator uploads buffers to the GPU in batches and waits on it less often. DREDGE on a PS4 Pro went from about 12 to 13–28 FPS, and 44–50 FPS in lighter views, and its sound no longer crackles.
- **A new emulator build** (KytyPS5 589bd14 with EmuFive patches 0001–0031): better memory use, GPU caches and shader translation, on top of the speed-ups above.
- **Smooth cover changes on the home screen.** Moving between games now changes the cover smoothly. Pick the effect in Settings, Appearance, Motion, Cover change. There are 11: fade, slide, zoom, wipe, dark, parallax, blinds, doors, push, iris and pixelate.
- **New PS4 Mesa.** The update installs the PS4 Mesa of PS4 Multiboot v1.5.0-beta-4, which is needed for all 4 GPU engines on the PS4 Pro (below).

### Update
1. Optional: copy `ps4-mesa.tar.xz` from [PS4 Multiboot v1.5.0-beta-4](https://github.com/blue0x1/ps4-multiboot/releases/tag/v1.5.0-beta.4) to `/user/home/` over FTP. The update takes it from there; without it, the PS4 needs to be online and downloads it (about 45 MB).
2. Settings, System, Software update. No restart is needed.

releases.name: v1.0.4
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.4

- Fixed: Software update in Settings did not start ("The update did not start.") (#16).
- Fixed: with EmuFive installed on a USB drive, games on a second USB drive were not found (#15).

### Updating from 1.0.3 or earlier

The old Software update cannot start, so start this update once by hand:

1. In EmuFive, turn on **SSH login** in Settings and connect the PS4 to the internet.
2. From a PC on the same network: `ssh ps5@<PS4 address>` (password `ps5` unless you changed it).
3. Run:
   ```bash
   sudo systemd-run --unit=emufive-update --collect /opt/ps5-on-ps4/bin/ps5-update install
   ```
4. Wait a few minutes, then restart from the home screen.

It installs every update you are missing (from 1.0.0 or 1.0.1 that includes 1.0.2's browser packages, about 110 MB). From 1.0.4 on, Software update in Settings works.

### New installs

`ps5-ps4-rootfs.tar.xz` below has 1.0.4 built in (install steps in the README).

releases.name: v1.4.0
releases.body:
# WWE '12 PC 1.4.0

The match-options update: new match rules in the menus (starting finishers, squash, I QUIT, Special Guest Referee), a Universe chaos level, Mod Maker additions and fixes for what you reported after 1.3.0.

## New match options

- **Starting finishers (as in WWE 2K14).** On the character select, press **LT / RT** on a place to choose how many finishers that wrestler starts with: NONE, 1, 2, 3 or INFINITE. It shows in the title of the attire frame (or in the READY banner for wrestlers with only one attire). Left on NORMAL, nothing changes. *Limit:* in a few match types the game skips the attire frame, so the option is only offered in a normal 1 on 1.
- **Squash matches.** In **OPTIONS > GAMEPLAY > BALANCING > DAMAGE** (the page now has three new lines): **SQUASH CHANCE** (0-100 %, the chance that a 1 on 1 match is a squash; 0 = off, the default), **SQUASH: JOBBER HEALTH** (starting health of the lower-rated wrestler, 20 % by default) and **STARTING FINISHERS** (default for every match). The lower-rated wrestler is the jobber; the other one starts with a finisher. The labels of the three new lines are in English only.

releases.name: v1.3.0
releases.body:
**WWE '12 PC v1.3.0 — "Speed and fixes"**

> ⚠️ No game data included: you need your own copy of WWE '12 for Xbox 360.

### Faster
- **Loading screens shorter** (a match loads in about 1.5 s instead of 4 s, the end of the entrances in about 1.9 s instead of 4.5 s). `wwe12_fast_loading = false` brings the old behaviour back.
- **Faster start-up** on PCs with 8 or more logical processors: the title screen comes after about 5-7 s instead of 15 s. On smaller processors the normal start-up is kept (`wwe12_fast_boot_min_threads`).
- **Sharper picture** when the game is drawn at 720p on a bigger screen (`svr_upscale_sharpness`, 0 turns it off).
- **Adaptive V-sync**: a late frame is shown at once instead of waiting a whole refresh (`svr_adaptive_vsync`).
- **Performance test** in the launcher (button *Performance test*): it plays a recorded 1-on-1 match with entrances once and tells you if your PC is fine, limited by the processor or by the graphics card. Nothing is changed without your agreement.

### Frame rate

**WWE '12 PC v1.2.0 — "Moveset update"**

> ⚠️ No game data included: you need your own copy of WWE '12 for Xbox 360.

### Fixed
- **Match-start stutter (and a short freeze) on integrated graphics (Intel...)**: the game's reads of the picture back from the graphics card are now grouped at the end of the frame (about 10 times less waiting at the start of a match). `svr_readback_defer_streak = false` goes back to 1.1.
- **Less work for the processor every frame** (helps small PCs, issue #53): shader constants are reused like on Android (`svr_reuse_constant_blocks`) and the check of 3D models is lighter (`svr_geometry_sample_min`, 32768 brings the 1.1 behaviour back).
- **Crash at start with file names that have accents or other characters** (for example a song called "Café.mp3" or a mod folder with Japanese letters in a mod): names are now read as UTF-8 everywhere in the game, the launcher and the Mod Maker, and a mod with an unreadable name is skipped instead of closing the game.
- **Launcher: the MUSIC page closed the launcher** when a file in the `music` folder had an odd name.

releases.name: v1.1.0
releases.body:
**WWE '12 PC v1.1.0**

> ⚠️ No game data included: you need your own copy of WWE '12 for Xbox 360.

### Fixed
- **Universe: crash with 5 or more matches per weekly show** (RAW / SmackDown set to 5 or 6 matches, especially in the weeks after some PPVs, and the show after WrestleMania). Fixed and tested over several simulated months.
- **Universe: the extra matches no longer repeat "#1 contender" matches** (the same wrestlers twice on one card), and a show set to 6 matches now gets its 6 matches week after week (the game's 7-day rest rule used to drop matches).
- **Direct3D 12 on older Intel graphics (UHD 620): half-transparent wrestlers and ring** fixed (#7). New setting `svr_d3d12_depth_flip` (true by default; `false` = 1.0 behaviour).
- **Damaged / white Superstar Threads attires on slower PCs** fixed (fix adapted from KaikoClanworth1's SvR 2011 PC port).
- **Direct3D 11: broken wrestler skin on old NVIDIA cards such as the GeForce GT 430** fixed (#55; fix adapted from KaikoClanworth1's SvR 2011 PC port).

releases.name: v1.0.0
releases.body: **WWE '12 PC v1.0.0**: 16:10 and ultrawide screens, a DirectX 11 version for older PCs, 360p/480p resolutions, a much bigger WWE Universe, a jukebox, and a Mod Maker that brings superstars, entrances and music from other WWE games. > ⚠️ No game data included: you need your own copy of WWE '12 for Xbox 360. ### New - 🖥️ **16:10 and ultrawide screens**: matches and entrances now fill the whole window (no more black bars on 1920x1200, 2560x1600, 21:9...). The HUD stays in the middle 16:9 area and the menus stay 16:9. Option in the launcher (SETTINGS > DISPLAY) and `wwe12_widescreen` in `wwe12.toml`; PICTURE FORMAT has AUTO / STRETCH. **Tested with Vulkan on 16:10 and 21:9 windows; the pause menu, the HUD in 21:9 and DirectX 11/12 are not fully checked: please tell us if something looks wrong.**

releases.name: Bachata S4 v0.2.5
releases.body:
PanVK V3, a global patch library, native NGS2 audio, and wide performance and compatibility fixes

## Highlights

- PanVK V3 3.2.0 ships for supported Mali GPUs, with faster God of War III textures.
- Global patch library with XML import, and new patches for more than a dozen games including P.T., Driveclub, UFC and Uncharted.
- Native NGS2 audio fixes Gravity Rush 2 audio glitches and silent dialogue, with a rewritten AJM path.
- Games folder prompt with autosync, a default save data location and in-game Pause.

## Game Compatibility & Patches

- Gravity Rush 2 audio now works properly: native NGS2 fixes the glitches and the silent dialogue
- P.T. renders streamed textures correctly, with checked 60 FPS, resolution, half-resolution shadow, lens flare, camera blur and SSR patches
- Driveclub 540p, 360p and high performance presets, with smoother frame pacing
- Second Son quality floor with a longer view distance and correctly lit scenes
- Galak-Z boots reliably and no longer deadlocks, and Elden Ring, UFC and Uncharted receive rendering and stability fixes
- Horizon Zero Dawn no longer runs out of memory when large buffers grow

releases.name: Bachata S4 v0.2.4
releases.body:
Uncharted and The Order: 1886 boot, Gravity Rush 2 optimizations, and PanVK for Mali

## Highlights

- Uncharted and The Order: 1886 now boot, with new graphics and resolution patches.
- Gravity Rush 2 optimizations and patches, including guarded low-resolution presets.
- PanVK driver support for a limited set of Mali devices.
- A proper two-finger touchpad, off by default and enabled from the in-game menu.

## Game Compatibility & Patches

- Uncharted boots, with fixed character rendering and new graphics and resolution patches
- The Order: 1886 boots, with rendering and stability fixes
- Gravity Rush 2 optimizations, guarded low-resolution presets, and a fixed mining movie transition
- Dark Souls Remastered and God of War III performance improvements
- Restored Bloodborne performance on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, and precise readbacks for Driveclub
- Synced the published patch catalog

## GPU Drivers

- PanVK V2 2.2.0 bundled as the production driver for supported Mali GPUs
- MediaTek devices default to PanVK where supported
- Faster memory budget queries and fewer redundant GPU barriers on PanVK
- Simplified Drivers screen with a single PanVK entry

releases.name: Bachata S4 0.2.3

Save Manager, expanded game compatibility, and new Adreno drivers

## Highlights

- Improved God of War III compatibility, graphics correctness, and performance.
- Added new patches and compatibility improvements for The Last of Us.
- Added Save Manager functionality for browsing, exporting, and importing game saves.
- Added the Turnip v5 driver and Vauzi drivers for Adreno 7xx-series chipsets.

## Game Compatibility & Patches

- Expanded God of War III compatibility with improved render-target handling and readback performance
- Fixed graphics issues that could cause screen whitening in God of War III

## Save Manager

- Added an in-app Save Manager for browsing installed game saves

releases.name: BachataS4 v0.2.2
releases.body:
# BachataS4 0.2.2

This changelog covers the work completed after the 0.2.0 release through 0.2.2.

## Highlights

- Added the native Android/Bionic runtime alongside the managed glibc/FEX runtime, with runtime-aware Vulkan driver selection.
- Added Storage Access Framework game folders, direct-folder launching, persisted folder permissions, and selective game removal/extraction flows.
- Added multilingual UI support, language settings, landscape orientation controls, touch profiles, controller themes, custom D-pad geometry, and a substantially improved touch-layout editor.
- Improved compatibility and performance for God of War III, The Last of Us, WipEout, and other titles through renderer, readback, image-layout, MSAA, and video-playback fixes.
- F-Droid and Play Store builds now ship the same six offline Turnip packages: three glibc drivers and three Android/Bionic drivers.

## Vulkan drivers and runtimes

- Added and qualified the native Android/Bionic host runtime.
- Added selectable glibc and Bionic runtime drivers with separate per-runtime profile selections.
- Preserved driver choices when switching runtimes and prevented incompatible ABI selections.

**Newer version:** [v0.5.5.3](https://github.com/ASEbrahim/MaliBridge/releases/tag/v0.5.5.3)

**English** · [简体中文](#zh-cn)

**Community:** [Discord](https://discord.gg/9xC67qTjDq) · [Support me on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/asebrahim)

**Download:** `DroidDeck-MaliBridge-v0.5.5.2.apk` (below, under Assets). Install it over v0.5.5.1, or from the app's **Updates** page: your games, settings and Steam login stay.

### Hotfix

- Your Proton choice for a game is no longer reset after a restart.
- Games that stop starting on Steam's Proton Experimental (ARM64) are moved to DroidDeck Proton by themselves, with a notice. This should fix Mad Max, Resident Evil 5, LEGO Indiana Jones and other games that broke after Steam's update (#55, Discussion #2).
- Games that wouldn't start after the app was force-closed start again.
- Should fix: the frame generation crash (ML-CNY7), and phones heating up on the Steam menu (ML-YEHM).
- Should fix: games closing on 11-12 GB phones, and OpenGL games like SOMA using too much memory (#50).
- Should fix: Sifu freezing and turning grey (ML-E72Q).
- Should fix: Steam's update screen looping into a full re-download (ML-D4P6).

releases.name: U24.07.02-2407
releases.body:
Notable changes from U24.03.22-21259

- Code refactoring and minor fixes
- Fixed a panic alert for Def Jam: Fight for New York and Fifa Street
- Numerous small optimizations to JitARM64
- Small optimizations to DSP HLE audio decoding
- Fixed stuttering from JIT Cache clear - mostly notable in Shadow the Hedgehog
- Set OSD message color to yellow in default AMOLED theme
- Updated Vulkan Memory Allocator and Vulkan Headers
- Updated and optimized app icons

Missing features - these features from Dolphin Official are not implemented

- Android Input Overhaul and subsequent changes to Input and TAS handling
- Custom GPU driver support
- Skylanders portal and Infinity base support
- Gamma correction

This codebase is based on the Official Dolphin dev build 2407-1 (Jul 2, 2024). For more information about what has changed check the PR history. 

**General information**
- When I started this project, my only goal was to add the VBI Skip hack to MMJR2. At the time, I had little to no coding experience and knew nothing about Git, GitHub, or Android Studio. Looking back to 2023, I never imagined I’d come this far.

releases.name: melonRA 0.5.1
releases.body:
# Changes (**Mainly bugfixes!**)
- Linux: Accepting a Netplay invite through Discord without having melonRA open would show an "Unknown protocol" error message, this was because it wasn't registered properly with the rest of apps in the OS, it now handles it properly.
- Netplay: Errors whilst syncing up instances and saves with the "hidden consoles" used for Netplay.
- Netplay: Closing the room closes the open UDP port after a while.
- Netplay: Closing a room with nobody connected is now instant.
- _Other minor Netplay fixes._
- Rewind kept its history after inserting a cartridge or booting up firmware. Meaning that, rewinding could make you rewind to a previous game. This has been patched.
- _Other general fixes._
- Casual mode offline unlocks were dropped if the saved login expired when its sent, now it is kept for the next login. And now the text is clearer when you play offline.

releases.name: melonRA 0.5.0
releases.body:
# Additions and changes
- There's a new and more concise **settings window** which shows all categories of settings in the same window without having to close and open them separately.
- **The name of the game is shown in the window title now, as well as its icon in the taskbar.**
- **"Hybrid Single"** as a new screen layout mode, literally the same as _Hybrid_, but without the mirroring of the top screen. _(Perfect for dyslexic people, like me! :D)_
- New **Time Played** and **Last Played** columns on the game list.
- **New option to mark games as "Favorite"** (it shows with a little heart besides the title, same place as the mastery and game settings cog) and a new tab for all favorite games.
- The ability to **make a desktop shortcut** for any game, which uses the actual icon of the ROM.
- **Thumbnails** for every save state slot.
- New option to **resume where you left off last session.** (Found in _Interface Settings_)
- New Rewind hotkey, must be enabled also in _Interface Settings_ alongside the amount of seconds you can rewind back to.
- **Trimmed the executable** so its a smaller download overall.

releases.name: melonRA 0.4.0
releases.body:
**NOTE:** As of today, 28/10, the emulator isn't yet verified for Hardcore completions in RetroAchievements' side. Some features might not be available just yet.

# Additions and changes
- **Discord Rich Presence** is now available, shows the emulator's name, the logo and header name of the ROM you are playing. When paired with RetroAchievements, shows details of their own Rich Presence on Discord (showing what you are doing in the game, the icon of the game's set, etc.)
- Some game list changes, including a new option **to display an achievement completion bar**, it'll turn gold when the game is Mastered. And it will show a little star in the title of the game, or in the cover when in grid mode.
- You can now right click games in the list and click "Achievements..." **it'll take you to that game's achievement page** where you can see your progress.
- A **hotkey to rotate the screens has been added** under Input and Hotkeys > General Hotkeys. Useful for games that require a lot of screen layout changes and rotation.

releases.name: melonRA 0.3.0
releases.body:
**NOTE:** As of today, 10/27, RetroAchievements hasn't yet verified the emulator for Hardcore support. So some features might not completely work as intended.

**NOTE 2:** Version no longer available because of updater changes for security reasons.

# Additions and changes
- **You can now unlock achievements whilst offline**, it will save the achievement data and will unlock them once it can reach the server again. (Both _Hardcore_ and _Casual_)
- Challenge indicators in the overlay are able to be **hovered on**, showing the requisites for the challenge itself and how many points its worth.
- **Quick screen layout and sizing hotkeys** (under _General Hotkeys_ in _Input and Hotkeys_ tab)
- **Game list has been optimised** so that it remembers your games already attributed, and only updates when it detects new ones or deletes when it doesn't see them in the directory.
- **Settings can now be exported and restored** from one system to another (excluding RetroAchievements login info)
- _Kaeru WFC_ and _Wiimmfii_ support in the **online play server picker** under _Wi-Fi Settings_

releases.name: melonRA 0.2.0
releases.body:
**NOTE:** Version no longer available because of updater changes for security reasons.

# Additions and changes
 - **Game list:** Now instead of the default melonDS starting screen, the emulator will prompt you to add a path for your games, and thus will put them in a modern, slicker game list that shows you the title of the game, its icon, region (and a flag!) and developer. 
 - The game list can be set to a **grid mode**, which will parse the covers of your downloaded library and make them appear uniformly in a square grid, you are able to change the sizing of this grid with a slider.
- **RetroAchievements sets** from your populated game list can all be viewed under "Achievements..." on the "RetroAchievements" tab. Your currently playing sits at the top showing all the subsets, whilst the rest are in a list to the side.
- **Overlay customisation:** you can now choose where elements are positioned in the screen under "Settings..." on the "RetroAchievements" tab. You will be able to choose where certain elements appear, and their visuals (such as having bolded text, making them smaller, or changing the colors to a simpler scheme)

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.5
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.5

Rewind, a cleaner Shifter and DMA sound, smoother audio recovery, and many usability fixes.

Try it in the browser, nothing to install: **[habib256.github.io/neost](https://habib256.github.io/neost/)**.

**What's new**
- **Rewind**: Ctrl+Alt+R steps back in time, floppies included (off by default).
- **Accuracy**: Closure runs clean (no stray black frames, no flickering borders); STE DMA sound, Shifter hardscroll, IKBD and serial chips closer to the real hardware; selectable master crystal.
- **Games**: Lemmings, Pacemaker, Obsession and Extase join the games replayed against Hatari (27 in total); TOS 1.06 US boots.
- **Usability**: picking a machine model also picks a matching TOS, and picking a TOS adjusts the model; a quieter terminal (`--verbose` for the full log); adaptive zoom fixed on Enchanted Land; a warm reset or a config change no longer scrambles Spectrum 512 pictures; twelve more keyboard layouts; keyboard joystick fires with right Alt/Option instead of right Ctrl (MacBooks have none); joystick dongles offered only on the port their game reads; bitmap explorer in the debugger; MIDI split and Time Code.

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.4
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.4

**What's new**
- **Accuracy**: MFP timers start on their own clock edge (Lethal Xcess on STE gets its top border back); MFP, ACIA, SCC and WD1772 closer to their datasheets.
- **Mouse**: drag-and-drop works in games and on the desktop; Chessmaster is now playable.
- **Games**: Lethal Xcess, Golden Axe, Rick Dangerous and Pang join the games replayed against Hatari (23 in total).
- **Verification**: a wider regression net (reference screens, game replays, the whole disk collection, Mega STE at 16 MHz) and a 68000 bench that now covers bus errors and double faults.

**Save states**: format v59, unchanged since 0.6.3.

Packages contain no Atari ROM: EmuTOS is the default. Licences included.

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.3 — NetUSBee USB and built-in networking
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.3 — NetUSBee USB and built-in networking

- **NetUSBee USB devices:** connect a virtual USB keyboard, mouse or disk image
  to either port. Hot-plug devices in Configuration → Network, save them in
  profiles, or use `--usb1` / `--usb2` in the headless runner. USB4TOS drivers
  have been tested with keyboard input, mouse packets and file reads/writes.
  Disk images support read-only mounting. Native ST-side USB drivers are required.
- **Built-in NAT:** IPv4/IPv6 networking without libslirp or GLib, including
  DHCP, DNS, TCP/UDP and explicit port forwarding. STinG/ENEC can load HTTP pages.
- **Hardware accuracy:** further CPU, video, floppy, serial and sound fixes,
  backed by chip documentation and regression benches. Vroom Elite starts on STE.
- **Issue #44:** missing Atari ROMs are reported as skipped Spectrum 512 tests;
  available machines still detect regressions, and partial runs cannot overwrite
  the reference set.

**Save states use format v59. Older states cannot be loaded.** Disk image contents
remain external to save states. USB passthrough and isochronous transfers are not
implemented.

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.2
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.2 — closer to the metal

Seven weeks of hardware fidelity work since 0.6.1.

**Deterministic external control.** A `--server` mode, joystick scripts, memory probes
and state exploration: the same script replays the same game down to the cycle. Disks
can be swapped while running and drive B unplugged from the server.

**Serial and keyboard chips rebuilt to match the hardware.** The MFP USART, the Mega STE
SCC, the MIDI and keyboard ACIAs, the IKBD protocol and the real-time clock. Custom 6301
keyboard programs are now recognised: *Froggies over the Fence* runs on all three disks.

**Floppies and hard disks.** More faithful STX copy protections, WD1772 write-protect
timing, and ACSI transfers that honour the DMA sector count.

**68881 FPU.** Transcendental functions are bit-exact.

**Video and memory.** STE 336-pixel mode, the 22-bit video counter wrap, the
"stopped Shifter" trick (resolution 3), and two new RAM sizes: 2176 KB and 2.5 MB.

**Sound.** The PSG crackle in *Super Hang-On* is gone, and STE DMA sound starts on the
exact sample of the PLAY write.

**Comfort.** Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen with mouse capture, mouse sensitivity is

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.1
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.1 — your settings stay put

A patch release. No new features: **23 defects** found and fixed across five rounds of multi-agent bug hunting, plus a hardware-validation pass on the published packages.

### Settings are saved again

On macOS and on every AppImage, NeoST runs from **read-only media**, so it stores its configuration in your user directory — but it never created that directory, and every setting was silently lost when you closed the emulator. **Five of the eight packages were affected.** Machine profile, video, audio and MIDI setup now survive a restart.

### Also fixed

- **The macOS disk image installs by drag and drop.** It shipped with the app alone, no `Applications` shortcut.
- **The web build ships its licences** (GPL-3.0, GPL-2.0, third-party notices), like every other package.
- **A save-state can no longer be reloaded under a different ROM.** The pairing relied on two bytes of TOS version, which five localisations share, so resuming under the wrong ROM froze the CPU without a word. The state format is now **v19**; v18 and older are refused explicitly, with a message that says why.

releases.name: DK64 Rekongpiled 1.0.3
releases.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Wondering about your save data when upgrading? Don't worry! Your save data is stored separately to the game itself. You can overwrite your old version and your save data will still be there, completely intact, and will work on the new version.

## Changelog
- Removed B Locker from extended draw distances, fixing a bug with being able to shoot the coconut switch in Hideout Helm lobby on higher draw distances
- Fixed a minor bug with sprite interpolation fixes where the matrix tag index of the sprite would overflow into unintended bounds
- Separated out options for gyro & mouse inversion. As such, you can now independently control which of these are inverted ( #73 )( #79 )
  - This now also impacts the controls of the cannon game in Gloomy Galleon
- Changed how the reduced lightning setting works ( #63 )( #89 )
  - Instead of reducing how intense a lightning strike is, instead it now reduces how frequently the flashes take place
  - This should remedy any remaining issues with this setting. As always though, there's about 500 different ways that DK64 can produce a lightning flash, so if we missed one, please let us know via a GitHub issue

## Changelog
### New features & non-bug fix changes
- Made the analog camera more responsive and less sluggish
- Extended the draw distance for some actors:
  - These actors tend to be non-enemy actors, since loading those from too far away can cause sigkill errors
- Disabled draw distance extension for melon crates
- Made the first person inversion option apply to Gyro & mouse controls
- Added in the ability to boot recomp via a CLI argument ( #55 )

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed an issue where a large spike in CPU load would permanently kill the audio engine until a program restart.
- Fixed an issue where disabled lightning would not work for some lightning events ( #30 )
- Fixed an issue where the game would leave zipper marks on the game during the open zipper animation
- Fixed an issue where the main menu scrolling background would look very weird on expanded HUD ( #42 )

releases.name: RomSieve 1.2.2
releases.body:
RomSieve 1.2.2 can write an archive that holds a single game as it is, instead of extracting its content: a disc image
of several gigabytes is neither decompressed nor compressed again. Your settings, profiles and journals stay as they
are, and a sort made with an earlier version can still be undone.

## New

### Preserve single-game archives

- **An archive written as it is.** The new option **Preserve single-game archives**, in the *Writing the files* frame of
  the **Output** step, writes a source archive (ZIP, 7z, RAR) as it is when it holds a single game (one file, or a
  descriptor and its tracks) and the sort keeps every file it holds. The archive is copied, moved or linked, according
  to the mode. An archive that holds one more file, such as a readme or a `.nfo`, has its content extracted, as before.
- **Named after its game.** The archive takes the name the DAT gives its file, with its own extension: `tetris.7z`,
  which holds `tetris.gb` identified as `Tetris (World).gb`, becomes `Tetris (World).7z`. The files it holds keep
  their names.
- **Counted as an archive.** The space needed on the destination and the FAT32 warning count the size of the archive,

releases.name: RomSieve 1.2.0
releases.body:
RomSieve 1.2.0 sorts a whole pack of DATs in one pass, reads DATs straight from their ZIP, 7z or RAR archive, and can
filter the files missing from the DAT by their name. Your settings, profiles and journals stay as they are, and a sort
made with 1.1.x or 1.0.x can still be undone.

## New

### A whole pack of DATs in one sort

- **Lot of DATs.** Choose a **folder** of No-Intro, Redump or TOSEC DATs (**Browse...**, then **Folder of DATs…**, or
  `--dat <folder>` on the command line) instead of a single DAT. The source is analysed once, each file is sorted with
  the first DAT that knows it, and each DAT keeps its own convention, filters and 1G1R. A lot may mix the three
  conventions.
- **DATs in an archive.** The DAT field also takes a **ZIP, 7z or RAR archive**, as downloaded, read without
  extracting anything. An archive of a single DAT (a Redump DAT) is that DAT; an archive of several DATs (a No-Intro
  daily pack, a TOSEC pack) is a lot.

releases.name: RomSieve 1.1.1
releases.body:
RomSieve 1.1.1 fixes how 1G1R handles games on several floppy disks in the No-Intro DATs, such as those of the Acorn
Archimedes. Your settings, profiles and journals stay as they are, and a sort made with 1.1.0 or 1.0.x can still be
undone.

## Fixes

- **Floppy disk sets kept together.** The No-Intro DATs of floppy disks number the disks `(Disk 1)`, `(Disk 2)`...,
  sometimes with a label: `(Disk 1, Game Disk)`, `(Disk 2 - Courses)`. RomSieve did not read these names as disks of
  one set, so 1G1R could keep some disks of a game and leave out the others. The disks of a set are now kept or left
  out together. Without a total in the name (`(Disk 1 of 3)`), the set counts as many disks as the highest number
  found.
- **Sets whose disks are clones of one disk.** These DATs describe each disk as a game and make the disks clones of
  one of them, so the set could lose to another release on the **Parent rather than clone** criterion. Such a set now
  counts as a parent.

releases.name: RomSieve 1.1.0
releases.body:
RomSieve 1.1.0 writes its ZIP archives in the **TorrentZip** format, the one RomVault and igir recognize. Your
settings, profiles and journals stay as they are, and a sort made with 1.0.x can still be undone.

## New

- **TorrentZip archives.** In the **ZIP** mode, each archive is now byte for byte the one that trrntzip, RomVault and
  igir write from the same files. The format fixes everything that could differ from one tool to another: the order
  of the files, their date, the compression and the headers. An archive therefore only depends on its content. A ROM
  manager takes a sorted collection as already in order, without compressing it again, and a collection shared with
  others stays identical from one user to the next. MAME sets and the software of MAME lists are still copied as
  they are, never compressed again.
- **Checked archives.** With **Verify copied files**, RomSieve also checks the TorrentZip signature of each archive,
  in addition to the content of each file. An archive that fails the check is deleted and the source is kept.

## Changes

- **The archives change.** An archive written by 1.1.0 is not byte for byte the one 1.0.x wrote for the same files,

releases.name: Linux beta 1: Seamless co-op
releases.body:
**Beta for testing.** This is a pre-release: the Windows launcher does not offer it as an update, and Windows players stay on 1.9.8.6.

## Seamless co-op on Linux

`Bloodborne-Linux-x86_64.AppImage` brings SuperMedo Seamless co-op (BBSC: Yharnam Together's co-op, by **CLSAMG22**) to the Linux version: native, no Wine. Make the file executable and open it.

- The launcher has a new **Seamless co-op** tab with its own Play button. The normal Play at the top still starts the normal game, and the Seamless co-op row on the Online page opens the new tab.
- It uses your SuperMedo account from the Online page: sign in there first.
- Host rules: enemies (normal, auto, a bit harder, harder, much harder, or your own health / damage / poise values from 1 to 10), boss tempo, rot, travel together with a vote, revive.
- Russia route for networks that cannot reach the SuperMedo server.
- Its own characters in `~/.local/share/bbport/seamless/user/savedata`, apart from your normal saves. Starting a new game is recommended. Your game folder is not changed: the co-op files are made in `~/.local/share/bbport/seamless`.

releases.name: Bloodborne PC 1.9.8.6
releases.body:
# Bloodborne PC 1.9.8.6

What's new since 1.9.8.4.

## Picture fixes
- **Smeared picture fixed (two causes):**
  - After a load, the game sometimes rewrote a command buffer it had already handed to the GPU. The picture then stayed broken or smeared until the game was restarted. Every submitted command buffer is now copied first (`BB_COPY_GPU_BUFFERS=0` turns this off). The same cause was behind "Unimplemented PM4 type 0" and "PM4 header ... rest of the buffer dropped" in logs.
  - After a start with an empty shader cache, one saved pipeline could be lost for the whole next session. The game's motion blur then kept blurring the last frame, so the picture looked smeared and frozen from the first camera turn on.
- Rainbow tiles on hit enemies and a light line along the top in cutscenes are fixed.

releases.name: Exiled-Kingdoms-Multiplayer-2.0
releases.body:
# 🛡️ [MOD] Exiled Kingdoms LAN Multiplayer — 2.0!

Hey everyone! Another update to the **LAN Multiplayer** mod for Exiled Kingdoms.

Here's the full summary:

---

## ⚔️ NEW — LAN Multiplayer Bug Fixes

### 🐛 Bug: Crash when entering Cities
- **Problem:** When entering some cities, the game would crash and close.
- **Fix:** Problem fixed, and you can now teleport and enter cities perfectly.

### 🐛 Bug: Monsters ignored the CLIENT when the HOST was far away
- **Problem:** Monsters only attacked when the HOST was nearby. If only the CLIENT approached, the monster would remain still.
- **Fix:** Detection now compares the HOST and all CLIENTs present on the same map and returns the **closest** to the monster as the target.

### 🐛 Bug: Incorrect monster level scaling in co-op
- **Problem:** Monsters scaled based on 0+ (extra players). × 2), resulting in level 2 Goblins in a session with 2
- **Correction:** Now uses the Bestiary's `minlevel` as a base before applying the LAN difficulty multiplier. Example: Goblin (base level 4) + 2 players = level 6. Yeti (base level 18) + 2 players = level 22.

### 🐛 Bug: CLIENT couldn't reduce HOST's HP in the PVP Arena

Essa release foi construída para entregar uma experiência mais divertida, mais estável e muito mais completa para quem sempre quis ver Exiled Kingdoms com um lado mais social e competitivo. --- ## 🔥 Destaques desta versão ### 🎮 Multiplayer Wi-Fi/VPN muito mais sólido O sistema multiplayer foi retrabalhado para oferecer uma experiência melhor em coop, com: - sincronização de sprites em tempo real - movimentação remota mais suave - Companion AI funcionando para clientes Wi-Fi/VPN - chat funcional com suporte multilíngue - sons espaciais de combate por proximidade - limpeza correta de peers desconectados - proteção contra corrupção de save **MODO LAN NO CANTO SUPERIOR DIREITO**

releases.name: X-OG Mobile v0.1.1

Pre-release debug APK for X-OG Mobile.

Changes since v0.1:
- Adds xemu Android block protocol androidfd: for SAF-selected game discs.
- Game ISO/XISO files are read from already-open Android file descriptors, without copying large disc images into app storage.
- Fixes launch failures on devices/vendors that deny reopening SAF-backed files through /proc/self/fd.
- Updates README files in English, Italian, French, German and Spanish.

Tested on HONOR BVL-N49: games launch from SAF-selected ISO/XISO without full-disc copying.

releases.name: X-OG Mobile v0
releases.body:
Initial proof-of-concept Android build of X-OG Mobile.

This is an experimental original Xbox emulator for Android based on a modified xemu core. It includes native Android UI, Vulkan video output, physical controller input, AAudio playback, game library scanning, pause/resume, and app-private system file setup.

No Xbox BIOS, MCPX ROM, HDD image, dashboard, or games are included. Users must provide legally obtained files.

Build type: debug APK.
Target ABI: arm64-v8a.
Minimum Android version: Android 10 / API 29.

releases.name: v0.10.65 — Rocky Ridge minecart above 60 Hz: the lever and the jump into the cart
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Rocky Ridge minecart above 60 Hz (#410, #401).** With **Test options › Gameplay › Race step rate** above 60 (for example 120 or 144):
  - **The cart's lever** no longer ends up hanging upside down under the cart when you lean left and right. At 144 Hz, each lean turned it about 2.4 times too far. After a few leans it had turned all the way round. It now stops where it does at 60 Hz.
  - **The jump into the cart** no longer flies too far. At 144 Hz the racer was put into the cart while still in the air. The jump now lasts about as long as at 60 Hz.
  - Both parts of the course moved by a fixed amount each step, an amount written for steps of one frame. They now move by the right amount for shorter steps. At the default 60 Hz nothing changes.

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.64](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.64).

## Validation

- **Windows x64 package, #410/#401: Rocky Ridge Expert, Sonic left to himself but leaning left and right in the minecart, at a Race step rate of 144 and 60:**
  - At 144 the lever stays upright in Sonic's hands the whole ride, as at 60.

releases.name: v0.10.64 — Expert courses above 60 Hz: the Final Factory skydive and the Metropolis Speedway launch
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Expert courses above 60 Hz (#410).** With **Test options › Gameplay › Race step rate** above 60 (for example 120 or 144):
  - **Final Factory Expert:** the skydive down the shaft no longer falls too fast or leaves the camera behind. At 144 Hz it fell about 2.4 times as fast, so the drop was over in about 2 seconds; it now lasts as long as at 60 Hz.
  - **Metropolis Speedway Expert:** the launch up the building no longer hangs at the top. At 144 Hz the racer stayed up there about 5.5 seconds instead of 3; it is now about 3.7 seconds.
  - Both were parts of the course that moved the racer by a fixed amount each step, written for steps of one frame; they now move by the right amount for shorter steps. At the default 60 Hz nothing changes.

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.63](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.63).

## Validation

- **Windows x64 package, #410, Sonic left to himself at a Race step rate of 144 and 60:**
  - Final Factory Expert skydive: falls at 97.4 units a second at 144 (60 Hz: 97.2; 0.10.63 at 144: 233.9), with the camera 17.4 behind the racer (60 Hz: 17.1; 0.10.63: 28.7).

releases.name: v0.10.63 — Older Mali phones no longer stop with a graphics error
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Older Mali phones (#406).** On phones with an older ARM Mali graphics chip, such as the Galaxy A05 and A06 (Mali-G52), the game no longer stops at start with "native graphics pipeline creation failed".
  - Their graphics driver refused every way of drawing a textured surface the game prepares, because of one feature the game asked for. The game now draws textures in a way that does not need it, and costs nothing extra.
  - Other phones, tablets and computers draw exactly as before.

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.62](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.62).

## Validation

- **Galaxy A06 (Mali-G52, the same chip as the A05), the fix's own build:** the graphics self test prepared all 455 ways of drawing (0.10.62: 71), drew with every one of them and read the picture back. This release's APK itself was not run on a Mali device.
- **AYN Thor (Adreno), this release's APK:** the same graphics self test prepared all 455 with none skipped and drew with all of them, so nothing changed on Adreno.

releases.name: v0.10.62 — The Forgotten Tomb launcher and the Final Factory pole above 60 Hz
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Races above 60 Hz: the Forgotten Tomb launcher and the Final Factory pole (#401).** With **Test options › Gameplay › Race step rate** above 60 (for example 120 or 144):
  - The big launcher in Forgotten Tomb, after the falling pillars, no longer throws you much too far. Before, a racer it carried moved 2.4 times too far each second at 144, so you landed well past the 60 Hz spot, and from the left side out of the course.
  - The pole you reach up and grab in Final Factory no longer ends its slide early, so you keep your momentum.
  - At the default 60 Hz nothing changes.

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.61](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.61).

## Validation

- **Forgotten Tomb on Windows, this release's package:** Sonic left to himself, same random seed at 60 and 144. Eight seconds after the launcher he was at height 162 at 144 (178 at 60; 90 with 0.10.61 at 144) and landed 15.2 seconds after take-off (17.0 s at 60; 13.0 s with 0.10.61 at 144). Full speed (0.999 at both rates).

releases.name: v0.10.61 — Board Super Sonic grinds rails, and races above 60 Hz behave
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Board Super Sonic grinds rails (#393).** With **General › Gameplay › Super Sonic: stay on the board** and **Super Sonic: all types on the board** both on, Super Sonic had the speed type but still rode past rails: the game's rail check skips Super Sonic. That one check now treats board Super Sonic like Sonic, so he jumps onto rails and grinds them like the computer racers do. Computer racers, online play and everything else are unchanged.
- **Races above 60 Hz behave (#392, #400, #401).** With **Test options › Gameplay › Race step rate** above 60 (for example 120 or 144):
  - Computer racers no longer fly off side ramps into the sky and stay there, so the place counter is right again. The fix for this has been in the source code since the option arrived in 0.10.50, but by mistake 0.10.50 to 0.10.60 were built without it; this release is built with it.
  - The camera now finishes moving from the starting view to the view behind your racer, instead of staying stuck halfway (wide angle, too far back), and it no longer flips over at ramps.
  - The camera follows at the same distance as at 60 Hz, instead of hanging too close.
  - At the default 60 Hz nothing changes.

releases.name: Nixport v1.2.304-alpha
releases.body:
**Nixport v1.2.304-alpha** — a test build for people who want to try it early.

> Published by hand: built and signed with the same key as v1.1.299-alpha and
> v1.0.267-alpha (upgrades install over them without uninstalling).

## Changelog (since v1.1.299-alpha)

### Gamepads

- **Single-player pad model** (replaces v1.1's player slots): exactly one physical
  pad feeds the game at a time. The pad you touch takes over automatically
  (last-active wins); the session drawer offers "use this pad" to pin a choice for
  the session. The effective pad and the on-screen controls merge into one player.

  sticks / D-pad / triggers now reach the game immediately at their current position —

releases.name: v1.2: cheats, new name and icon
releases.body:
**Cheats, under CTRL** (requested in #1).

- **Infinite EP:** EP stays at its maximum, so Teleport, Chronostasis and every other EP ability cost nothing.
- **Freeze the clock:** the game's clock stands still, so the days do not pass.

Both are off by default. Tap **CTRL** at the top of the screen, scroll down to *Cheats*, tick what you want and tap **Apply**: they take effect at once, without a restart, and stay set for the next start. A save made while a cheat is on keeps its effects (a frozen clock stays at its time).

**New name and icon:** the app is now called **LR:FFXIII** on your home screen and in the app drawer, with the game's emblem as its icon.

**Updating from v1.1:** install `lr-recomp-android-arm64.apk` (below) over it. Your saves, game files and shaders are kept. If you downloaded v1.2 in its first hours (still named *Lightning Returns Recomp*), install it again for the new name and icon; nothing else changed.

releases.name: v1.1: download the APK
releases.body:
**Download the APK, pick your ISO, play.** No PC needed any more.

1. Install `lr-recomp-android-arm64.apk` (below) on your device.
2. Put an ISO of your own **USA** disc of *Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII* on the device.
3. Start the app and tap **Import from ISO…** on the *Game folder* page (keep the bundled Turnip driver if the GPU driver page comes up). When the import is done, tap **Start game**.

**The first start takes a few minutes, with the progress on screen** (times from the AYN Thor): about 45 s of *Loading…*, about 45 s of *Preparing shaders* (the game waits; hold START + BACK for 2 s to skip), then about 3.5 minutes of *Compiling the remaining shaders* in the corner of the title, where you can already play (starting the game pauses it until the next start). Later starts are quick and don't stutter.

releases.name: v1.0: first public release
releases.body:
First public release of the source.

**No APK is attached, on purpose.** The APK contains code generated from the game's executable, so you build your own from your own copy of the game. See the README: one command, `tools/quickstart.sh`.

Highlights:
- A second screen on dual-screen devices such as the AYN Thor: schemata, enemy weaknesses and EP in battle, and an area map that follows the camera in the field.
- 30, 40 or 60 fps in gameplay, measured in the Thor's lowest power mode (Standard) on the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2.
- The Turnip GPU driver is bundled, shaders are precompiled at the title screen, and the game can be imported from an ISO on the device.

Attached: a 2-minute video recorded on the AYN Thor, both screens at 60 fps, in 1080p and a smaller 720p version. Screen recording costs some frame rate, so judge performance by the README's numbers, not by this video.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.5-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.5-dev (versionCode 9).

### Changes

- Added native implementations of selected game, rendering, AI and container algorithms, with the original recompiled paths retained. Optimized guest-register handling, x87 calculations and indirect-call caches.
- Added Optimal (ARM64) and Exact (x86) execution modes. Exact selects the original recompiled algorithms; both modes run as ARM64 code.
- Reduced GLES state traffic between threads, draw preparation work and shader constant uploads, and improved shader program caching.
- Improved launcher operation progress, diagnostics and Play button feedback, with the amber UT3 palette.
- Added an optional 4 GB guest address space, enabled by default on 64-bit devices with at least 5 GiB of RAM.
- Fixed fingerprint sensors being mistaken for gamepads.
- Reduced APK size by stripping non-runtime library symbols while retaining the original library for offline profiling. Expanded regression tests and updated documentation.

### Requirements

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.4.1-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4.1-dev (versionCode 8).

### Changes

- Improved CPU performance on PhysX Mod Pack maps with native fluid collision kernels, native pair removal and optimized x87 calculations.
- Added on-device HLSL compilation through vkd3d-shader, with shader caching and improved MojoShader compatibility for mod materials.
- Fixed touch aiming: holding Fire no longer blocks another finger's camera movement; dragging from Fire, secondary fire, Jump or Crouch also turns the camera.
- Made the crash monitor a launcher option, disabled by default, to avoid keeping its extra Android process running unless needed.
- Removed FSR3 frame generation. FSR1 spatial upscaling and FXAA remain available.
- Reduced per-draw post-processing overhead and removed temporary qa-flags performance switches.
- Updated localized PhysX and audio setting descriptions.

### Installation and validation

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; compatible Adreno devices can use Turnip.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.4-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4-dev.

### Changes

- Added an FPS counter with a frame-time graph and optional system information for every renderer.
- Added FSR1, FXAA, and FSR3.1 frame generation (DXVK, Android 12+; disabled by default).
- Added CPU-based PhysX effects and OpenAL Soft audio through AAudio with EAX 1–5 support.
- Added a maximum-graphics button and fixed persistence of the 3D rendering scale.
- Fixed terrain rendering in OpenGL ES, accelerated DXT decoding, and allowed unused texture mip levels to stream out.
- Improved GPU query handling in GLES and DXVK, including on PowerVR devices.
- Fixed ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion on shared storage on Pixel devices.
- Added a “Firing or aiming” gyroscope mode and persistent crash reports with a separate error window.

### Installation and limitations

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; frame generation requires Android 12+. Frame generation may cause HUD artifacts and adds GPU and memory overhead. A stable 60 FPS at maximum graphics settings is not guaranteed.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.3-dev
releases.body:
The third release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 improves GLES performance, text editing and graphics cache handling.

### Changes

- Added a dedicated GLES render thread with automatic CPU core selection. Streamed draw uploads, asynchronous query polling and shader program prelinking reduce work on the game thread.
- Added driver-aware graphics cache maintenance: GLES program binaries are invalidated after driver changes, and DXVK keeps the current and newest other pipeline cache for each driver.
- Fixed DXVK scaled vertex formats with a shader fallback for drivers that need it.
- Replaced keyboard-only text entry with an Android editing dialog for game fields, console commands and chat. Existing text can be corrected or cleared; cancellation preserves it, and original character filters remain in effect.
- Added separate weapon-button swipe settings and expanded the in-game Android settings to nine languages: English, Russian, Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian and Polish.
- Improved launcher texture status and fixed texture handling, audio and FSINCOS translation. Expanded regression tests and rendering diagnostics.

### Requirements

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 0.2-dev
releases.body:
The second release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 adds optional texture conversion, more flexible touch controls, OpenSpy compatibility and save/profile fixes.

### Changes

- Added optional ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion in the launcher, including games played directly from stored ZIP archives. Original packages are retained; runtime DXT decoding remains available for cache misses and mods.
- Added a touch layout editor to move, resize and hide individual controls. Hold the on-screen Pause button to open it; a short tap opens the original pause menu.
- Expanded touch settings with a fixed joystick, weapon tap/swipe selection, separate weapon bar/wheel sizes, control visibility, movement while holding primary fire and horizontal gyro reversal.
- Added OpenSpy service and authentication compatibility, and fixed a registry-call crash during online play.
- Prevented startup defaults from overwriting saved profiles and campaign progress before sign-in. Fixed creation of save directories beneath virtual ZIP folders.

releases.name: typex2-recomp 0.3.1
releases.body:
Faster on Android, and Load State fixed in RetroArch.

- **Android:** games run faster. Game code is now built with link-time
  optimisation, and calls between its parts are cheaper. **The King of
  Fighters XIII Climax** holds 60 fps in fights on every stage tested on
  the test tablet; before, most stages ran at about 50.
- **Save states in RetroArch:** Load State works with RetroArch's "Undo Load
  State" backup (on by default), which the core used to refuse silently.
  After a game's movie, saving and loading no longer pause the game for a
  second.


**Known issues:** [docs/Known-Issues.md](https://github.com/PabloVSouza/typex2-recomp/blob/main/docs/Known-Issues.md)

releases.name: typex2-recomp 0.2.0
releases.body:
The launcher becomes the Android app, and games' code travels as packs.

**Updating the Android app: uninstall the old one first.** The new Type X2
app is signed with the project's release key, so Android refuses to install
it over an older Type X2 app. Your saves and settings are in your game
folders and stay.

1. On the device, uninstall **Type X2**: long-press its icon → App info →
   Uninstall (or Settings → Apps → Type X2 → Uninstall).
2. Install `typex2-android.apk` from this release and open it. Allow "All
   files access" when it asks: it reads your ROMs folder and writes each
   game's `x2.env`.
3. In the launcher on your computer, Export → **Game packs for the Android
   app** with your games, then **Send to device** (USB debugging on). Or
   copy the `x2-*.so` files to `Android/data/com.typex2.recomp/files/packs`
   on the device.
4. Open the app again: it installs the packs and lists your games. ES-DE
   launches them as before.

releases.name: typex2-recomp 0.1.1
releases.body:
Smoother games, RetroArch Reset, and a launcher that tells you about updates.

**Frame pacing:** steadier in every game. The games' own frame
timers no longer fight the runtime's, and their worker threads no longer
wake each other for nothing. BlazBlue's late frames dropped by half or more.

**Android:**

- RetroArch: Reset restarts the game.
- BlazBlue Calamity Trigger: a shorter pause at fight start.
- KOF XII: bold text is bold again.

  OpenGL ES is no longer a supported fallback.

**macOS:** KOF XII's left credit counter shows "00" again.

**Launcher:** tells you when a new version is out, with the release notes
and a link to the downloads (About → Updates turns it off).
